_note: RI-WLD16's reference artifact in machine-readable form: the landform grammar of the thirteen regions. Each region declares a macro-form class, a drainage pattern, a bedrock/soil, and the named landform elements a walk through it must cross. `measured_*` fields are the shipped tree at commit cf2755a via corpus/80-methods/m-wld16-landform-census.mjs — they are the BASELINE, not the target. Provenance per field is in RI-WLD16 §Provenance note.

western-rootlands.bedrock: peat over white limestone; the limestone surfaces only where a root has lifted it
landform_elements: root-levee (the road itself, 1.5-3 m above the backswamp)
crevasse splay where a levee has burst
nest-mound (built, but reads as landform at distance)

eastern-rootlands.bedrock: none exposed; unconsolidated tidal mud to depth
eastern-rootlands.soil: tannin-black silt, firm at low tide and SUCK at high
landform_elements: mud bar exposed only at low tide

blackwood.bedrock: white Ayleid-quarried limestone, karstic — the ruins are made of the country rock
blackwood.soil: leaf-litter over rendzina; thin, and it shows as bare stone on every steep face
landform_elements: blind valley where a stream vanishes into rock

hive.bedrock: irrelevant — the surface is comb, and the comb is the landform
hive.soil: wax and chitin-meal; no mineral soil at all
landform_elements: collapse pit into a spent cell

marauders-coast.bedrock: shell-hash conglomerate (coquina), which is what the bone-scaffolds are footed on
marauders-coast.soil: salt-grass over barnacle shelf; SUCK below the high-water line
landform_elements: tidal pan that floods on the 12-minute clock

stone-forest.bedrock: silicified wood in a tuff matrix — the petrified trees ARE the outcrop
stone-forest.soil: thin sandy loam between the boles; bare tuff on the risers
landform_elements: tuff riser (a 3-8 m step you must find a way up)

salt-hills.bedrock: bedded gypsum and marl; the Imperials quarried the marl and left the gypsum
salt-hills.soil: hill grass over stony rendzina, salt-crusted in the hollows
landform_elements: pass saddle (the only crossings, and the ambush sites)

valus-ridge.bedrock: wind-holed limestone (the rock flutes) over folded slate
valus-ridge.soil: almost none; cliff-lichen directly on rock, hanging moss on the north faces
landform_elements: cloud shelf (the bench where cloud sits below you)

thornmarsh.bedrock: buried; ash-dusted peat dome over it
thornmarsh.soil: acid peat, ash-dusted grey on every upward surface
landform_elements: bog dome (you are walking uphill without seeing it)
lagg (the wet moat at the dome's edge)
ash drift on the windward side

clay-moor.bedrock: fired red clay over shale; the naga kilns are cut into the outcrop
clay-moor.soil: none worth the name — sparse scrub on a hardpan

crimson-coast.bedrock: red mudstone; the lichen took its colour cue from the rock and then exceeded it
landform_elements: lichen shelf at the high-water mark

deep-marshes.bedrock: drowned xanmeer masonry is the only hard surface in the region
deep-marshes.soil: voriplasm-bearing black mud; the ground is an animal (RI-WLD11)

stone-wastes.soil: salt-crust; glass-thorn roots find whatever is under it and nothing else does
